title: Public sector permitting chatbot pilot - SOW and workshop brief
body:
Summary:

Quick working draft SOW and workshop brief for a 6-week pilot with a city permitting office to validate a chatbot assistant for: permit lookup, application checklist guidance, and simple status checks. Goal is to demonstrate reduction in first-line support volume and improve citizen self-service. This doc is intentionally lightweight — use as the basis for the kickoff workshop and commercial estimate.

Background / context:
- Customer: mid-sized US city (planning + permitting office). High seasonal volume, many repetitive questions (zoning rules, required docs, status checks).
- Customer wants a lightweight, privacy-friendly pilot deployed in their cloud (VPC) or Redwood Dedicated depending on security review.
- Key constraints: PHI not present but PII (addresses, names) will be referenced; must support audit logs and retention controls.

Objectives (pilot success criteria):
1) Accurate answer rate >= 70% on a curated set of 400 citizen FAQs measured via manual evals and live-sampled transcripts.
2) Average human deflection >= 20% for supported intents during the pilot per week.
3) End-to-end response P95 latency <= 850ms for standard queries from city region.
4) Integration proof-points: connectivity to permitting status API (read-only), fine-grained audit logs.

Scope (in-scope):
- 6-week pilot (plus 1-week discovery and 1-week wrap). Total engagement window 8 weeks.
- Deliver a chat UI prototype (hosted by customer or Redwood demo UI) + Redwood-hosted inference endpoint and a simple middleware connector to customer permitting API (read-only).
- Data handling: ephemeral KV cache and optional request-level redaction rules; logs forwarded to customer SIEM.
- Evaluation set creation: joint 400-question set (city + Redwood), baseline run, weekly quality checks.
- Workshop: kickoff (discovery), mid-pilot review, final demo + handover.

Out of scope:
- Full ticketing system integration or two-way permit state mutations (no create/update on permit records).
- Deep NLP model fine-tuning on private documents (we will use prompt engineering + retrieval augmentation; fine-tune possible as a follow-on item).
- Complex multi-step workflows (e.g., complete permit submission flows) unless scoped in follow-on.

Deliverables:
- Discovery notes & integration checklist (1 week)
- Working prototype: chat UI + backend connector + Redwood inference config (3 weeks)
- Eval report with metrics, 400-question annotated set, and tape of representative conversations (week 5)
- Ops handover doc: runbook for failover, monitoring dashboard screenshots, audit log schema (week 6)
- Final demo and recommendation playbook (week 7 wrap)

Staffing (typical):
- Solutions Eng lead (Maya) - overall PO/technical lead (10 days total)
- Backend engineer (connector) - 15 days
- Prompt & retrieval engineer - 12 days
- Customer success / project manager - customer side coordination (shared)
- Optional: Security review consultant for VPC/on-prem checklist (3 days)

High-level timeline (weeks from kickoff):
- Week 0: Discovery workshop (2h) -> finalize integration checklist, data access permissions
- Week 1: Environment setup, baseline eval (collect sample transcripts), connector scaffolding
- Week 2-3: Prototype dev, retrieval index with city public docs, prompt cycles
- Week 4: Internal QA, synthetic load tests, mid-pilot workshop to show baseline metrics
- Week 5-6: Iterate on quality, deploy to limited public beta (internal city staff), collect metrics
- Week 7: Final demo, handover, recommendation and pricing for production roll (if requested)

Workshop agenda (discovery kickoff, 2 hours):
- 0:00-0:10 Introductions, objectives & success criteria
- 0:10-0:25 Current process walkthrough (city ops) — ticket volumes, typical question types
- 0:25-0:45 Data & integrations — which APIs, SSO, audit logging expectations
- 0:45-1:05 Privacy & security constraints — PII handling, retention, IP concerns
- 1:05-1:25 Live transcript review — select 20 representative queries, map to intents
- 1:25-1:50 Pilot plan, timeline, roles/responsibilities, immediate blockers
- 1:50-2:00 Next steps and action items

Pricing (ballpark, indicative only — subject to final security/network scoping):
- Fixed professional services for pilot (discovery, connector, prompt engineering, evals, handover): $45k - $65k (one-time).
- Infra estimate options (6-week pilot):
  - Redwood Hosted (shared): $6k - $9k (includes inference usage at expected volume)
  - Dedicated small pool (reserved for pilot, better latency/SLA): $18k - $25k (6-week pro-rata)
- Optional add-ons: extra data engineering for doc ingestion $6k, on-prem packaging / air-gap assessment $10k - $18k, security consultancy $4k.

Assumptions behind pricing:
- Pilot will use a retrieval-augmented generation approach with a moderate-size open model variant (no costly fine-tune).
- Query volume during pilot estimated at 15k queries total (avg 750/day over a 20-working-day exposure).
- Customer will provide read-only API access and a corpus of public-facing docs (zoning regs, checklists) in week 0.
- Network/VPN access for connector work available during week 1; if not, extra time/cost may apply.

Success metrics and monitoring:
- Weekly dashboard: accurate-answer-rate, human deflection rate, response latency P95, fallback rate ("handled by human"), number of escalations.
- Post-pilot recommendation: feasibility to move to production (yes/no), recommended infra (hosted vs dedicated), estimated monthly run cost and 6-month ROI calc (credits/time saved).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Sensitive PII leaking in logs. Mitigation: redact rules, token-level redaction, forward logs to customer SIEM, short retention in Redwood console for pilot.
- Risk: Permitting API rate limits / flaky endpoints. Mitigation: caching layer, retries, synthetic test harness.
- Risk: Quality low on edge-case regulatory questions. Mitigation: focus pilot on 400 high-value FAQs; escalate complex questions to human queue; log for model improvement.

Open questions (to clarify in kickoff):
- Which hosting mode allowed per procurement (Hosted API, Dedicated, VPC/private)?
- Permitting API spec + auth method (API key, OAuth, mutual TLS)?
- Expected daily peak traffic and SLA targets for production (post-pilot)?
- Are there existing canned FAQ lists or help center articles we can index?

Deliverable format & handoff:
- All artifacts delivered as markdown + Redwood Console snapshots.
- Connector code pushed to customer repo or a shared sandbox repo with PR; detailed deployment README included.
- Final recommendations doc to include cost/latency trade-offs and suggestion for production rollout phases.

Next steps (owner in parens):
1) Confirm pilot approval and PO (City legal) (Customer)
2) Schedule kickoff workshop; share sample transcripts + API spec before workshop (Maya / Customer)
3) Security pre-check (VPC vs hosted decision) (Rajan)
4) Draft final SOW and commercial terms after workshop (Maya)

Notes / TODO (working):
- Add high-level sample prompts and retrieval templates here after kickoff.
- Prepare a short red-team checklist for potential PII exposures.
- Consider a small supervised fine-tune if accuracy on regulatory Qs is below 60% at week 4 (treat as change request).

-- end of brief.
